glossary.definition: One long-lived token the agent holds for days or weeks. A captured copy stays useful until it expires - the standing risk.
A credential minted at request time for one call: short TTL, tool-bound scope. A captured copy is dead within minutes.
The credential names the one tool it may call. Even within its short life it cannot be replayed against a different tool.
Time to live: how long a credential works. The lab compares 30 days (standing) against 300 seconds (JIT) at capture + minutes-to-hours.
A token an attacker copied at time T. The only question that matters: is it still useful at T + N? Short TTLs shrink that window to nothing.
Revoking a tool at the issuer refuses even a fresh JIT credential for it - revocation and TTL are independent controls.
